notes: The pre-state CLI only prints usage and exits 2; src/store.mjs does not exist. T1 creates saveItem in src/store.mjs and replaces the CLI stub with the add branch, the usage branch, and one try/catch. The CLI joins the arguments after add with one ASCII space (D4, A5), calls saveItem, then prints exactly saved plus a newline. T1 intentionally accepts blank names until T2. The list command remains a usage error until T3. Unknown commands keep the existing usage text and exit code 2. No dependency is added.

Storage is settled by D2 and A1: one JSON object {"name":"<name>"} per line in data/items.jsonl. The module chooses process.env.ITEMS_FILE when non-empty, otherwise new URL("../data/items.jsonl", import.meta.url). An override is used as given, relative to the working directory. T1 saveItem(input) trims input and synchronously appends JSON.stringify({name}) + "\n" with appendFileSync; it returns only after that write. The data directory already exists through data/.gitkeep. The default data file is gitignored. The small store module owns both the path and the full name rule so add and list cannot choose different files.

T2 changes only src/store.mjs. After trimming, saveItem rejects an empty name or any remaining U+000A or U+000D by throwing Error("item name must not be blank") before writing; all other characters remain unchanged. An absent add argument reaches saveItem as the empty string. T1 already implements the CLI catch: print error.message followed by a newline to stderr, set process.exitCode = 1, and return. No path calls process.exit; usage sets exitCode = 2, successes leave it 0, and Node drains stdout before exit.

T3 adds listItems in src/store.mjs and the list branch in src/cli.mjs. That branch accepts no arguments; extra arguments take the existing usage-error branch (A7). listItems reads the file as UTF-8, returns [] for ENOENT or an empty file, and rethrows all other errors. For nonempty content it splits on "\n", removes only the last empty element if present, parses every remaining line with JSON.parse, and returns each name in file order. The CLI writes each returned name followed by "\n", or nothing for []. Parsing completes before any list output. T3 follows T2 so its regression checks include the completed name rule.

No recovery, locking, retry, fsync or journal is added: those address the stated non-goals. A damaged JSON line makes list fail through the CLI catch without partial output. One process uses the file at a time (A3); saved means appendFileSync returned, not durability after power loss.

Each check runs commands in separate processes. item-add checks whitespace trimming, unquoted multiword joining, persistence and exact saved output using data/check-items.jsonl. Its default case copies src/ into a disposable application with its own empty data/, invokes that copy from outside its directory with ITEMS_FILE unset then empty, and checks its two stored items. item-blank checks spaces, no argument, LF and CR, the exact stderr message and exit 1, no stdout, and no persisted item. item-list checks an empty list, two names in order, both default-path branches in a disposable application, read/parse errors (A6), and the usage error for extra list arguments (A7). Each override check resets only data/check-items.jsonl in its first case. No check touches a person's default data file (A4). Each protected check gets a fresh checkout from the gate, and its cases run in array order; different checks do not share their data file.

Task risks and mitigations: T1 could select the wrong default file, preserve unwanted whitespace, or drop unquoted words; item-add tests each, including both unset and empty overrides outside the temporary application directory. T2 could reject valid names or turn invalid input into an unrelated failure; it reruns item-add and item-blank verifies the exact error, status and unchanged store. T3 could use a different default or hide a read/parse error as an empty list; item-list exercises those failures and verifies no partial stdout. No other external system or permission is involved.

tasks.title: Save an item
tasks.goal: `add <name>` persists the named item and prints `saved`
tasks.exitCondition: item-add passes: trimmed and multiword names persist through the override; unset and empty ITEMS_FILE select the isolated application's default store

tasks.title: Reject a blank name
tasks.goal: `add` with a blank name reports the error on stderr, exits 1 and persists nothing
tasks.exitCondition: item-blank passes and item-add still passes

tasks.title: List saved items
tasks.goal: `list` prints every saved item, one per line, in the order saved
tasks.exitCondition: item-list passes, and item-add and item-blank still pass
